The CI failure was caused by contract validation (`ARCH-4`) on downstream consumers (`analytics-ingest` and `billing-service`) which still require `placedAt` and `totalCents` respectively.

To support both the new field names (`createdAt` and `amountCents` aligned with Payments & Customer APIs) and backwards compatibility with existing consumers, `OrderPlaced` now provides both sets of fields.

### Changes Made

1. **[`src/core/events.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w1/r/src/core/events.ts)**:
   - On [`OrderPlaced`](file:///C:/avg/w1/r/src/core/events.ts#L7-L30), included `createdAt` and `amountCents` while retaining `placedAt` and `totalCents` for downstream compatibility (ARCH-4).
   - In [`orderPlaced`](file:///C:/avg/w1/r/src/core/events.ts#L46-L67), populated both `createdAt` and `placedAt` with `order.placedAt`, and both `amountCents` and `totalCents` with the order total.

2. **Tests**:
   - Updated **[`test/app.test.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w1/r/test/app.test.ts#L21-L54)** and **[`test/adapters.test.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w1/r/test/adapters.test.ts#L46-L55)** to assert both the new (`createdAt`, `amountCents`) and legacy (`placedAt`, `totalCents`) fields on published `OrderPlaced` events.

### Verification
- `npm run typecheck` passed with 0 errors.
- `npm test` passed all 39 tests across 13 suites.
- `npm run arch` passed dependency-cruiser checks.
